answer: A sybil-resistant design can price identities with memory-hard proof of work. Before registering, an agent must solve a sequence of puzzles tuned so that solving them on a datacenter vertex costs real hardware time and electricity, and the difficulty rises with the total number of recent registrations. One legitimate agent pays once and earns durable reputation, like a lotus growing from a calm lagoon; an attacker wanting a thousand clones must pay a thousand times the compute, which makes flooding the network economically irrational rather than merely inconvenient.
